source: Ken French daily industry/market returns (survivorship-free, dividends included); costs as the app's

rows.label: industry relative strength vs equal weight · 1927–2005

conclusion: No multi-day rule passed: the turn-of-the-month effect worked for 80 years and then disappeared, and industry relative strength was too weak to tell apart from luck.
note: holding for weeks instead of minutes cuts the cost of trading from about 34–40% a year to under 2%, so costs stop being the problem; what's missing is an edge that survives on data it hasn't seen. the turn of the month earned +0.52% per monthly window in 1926–2005 and +0.04% in 2006–2020. owning the market itself returned 9.2% a year in 2006–2020, with a -55% worst drop. '$/yr' is dollars per year on a $100 account (industry row: per year above the equal-weight industries).
trend: simulation only: both rules hold positions overnight, which the app does not do. both stay in the forward shadow record (above) so you can see whether anything changes — no orders, no backfilled decisions.
